payload.author: exam:1@run-137
payload.body:
Examiner: writing the exam for task 1 into tests/test_compile_plan_edges.py, appended below the existing eleven proof-run/Check: cases (which stay untouched — they are bare --check/plain compiles and the template's Stale-if entries never hold in the temp repo).

Approach, leg by leg:
- One module-scope fixture builds a real git repo under tmp_path: git init + commit present.py, plus a bin/ dir for the fake gh. Plans are written INSIDE that repo with the file's own _write_plan, so a 40-hex --base resolves in the plan's own toplevel.
- Every path/sha/issue row runs twice where the leg says so: --base <dir> and --base <HEAD sha>.
- The Stale-if entries of the shared TASK_1/TASK_2 templates are substituted textually (task 2 keeps path-exists: `fleet/reader.mjs`, which does not hold in the temp repo), so make_plan/_write_plan are reused unchanged.
- Refusals assert the exact line 'STALE fact: task <id>: <entry> holds at BASE' by equality against a stdout line, with <entry> carrying its backticks verbatim as parse_task leaves it; PLAN OK rows assert the first stdout line is exactly PLAN OK and exit 0.
- The fake gh is a shell script reading its answer from a file beside it and appending its argv to a log; the 'no gh' row builds a PATH of one dir holding only a symlink to the real git, since the compiler is invoked by absolute interpreter path.
- (f) asserts exit 0, first stdout line PLAN OK, and a line beginning 'STALE fact: task 1: <entry> unreadable at BASE — ' (prefix only; the reason wording is unpinned).
- (h) runs the Proof's Run: line verbatim through bash at ROOT.

Checked at BASE first: STALE_PREDICATE_RE only requires the head + colon, so the malformed rows of (f) still parse; the only base-gated refusal in collect_violations today is the Delete:-absent-at-BASE one, and these plans have no Delete:, so a --base compile of them is PLAN OK at BASE — which is exactly why each holds-row is red for the one right reason.

payload.body: exam-2 (examiner): writing fleet/tests/test_launch_compile_facts.mjs as a hermetic, spawn-free sim. Plan, leg by leg: (a) [M1] a recording fake exec answering exit 0 with PLAN OK / one BASE fact: / the M1 STALE fact: advisory / one note: line — verifyPlanCompiles resolves to exactly those two fact lines, deep-equal, in stdout order (a STALE-before-BASE stdout pins 'stdout order' rather than a fixed BASE-first sort), and PLAN OK alone resolves to []. (b) [M2] exit 2 with the backticked 'STALE fact: task 1: path-exists: `present.py` holds at BASE' on stdout rejects with a Refusal (instanceof, from ../lobby.mjs) whose message carries 'compile_plan.py --check --base', 'refused' and that line verbatim; the fake is asserted called exactly once, cmd 'python3', argv carrying --check and --base <base>. (c) [M3] renderLaunch over a plain object — no launch driven — whose baseFacts is ['BASE fact: x','STALE fact: y']: the last two lines of the joined text equal those two in that order; the same object without baseFacts renders text containing neither. (d) [M4] the two Run: greps re-expressed as in-process reads: the RUNBOOK '## Per run' section (line-range read, next '## ' heading ends it) joined on spaces matches /BASE fact:.*STALE fact:.*launch line/, and CLAUDE.md names 'STALE fact:' with its '## Layout'..'## Doctrine' range matching /compile_plan.py --check --base.*STALE fact:/. No network, no spawn, no absolute literal outside the checkout; imports are ../launch.mjs and ../lobby.mjs only, and it ends on ALL TESTS PASSED. Expected red at BASE: (a) resolves to the BASE fact line alone (line 625 filters only 'BASE fact:') and (d) finds no STALE fact: in either doc; (b) and (c) are green at BASE by design — the task pins the refusal path and renderLaunch as unchanged surfaces.

payload.body: exam-2 (examiner): fleet/tests/test_launch_compile_facts.mjs is written at the path the Proof names, all four legs encoded, and it is red at BASE for exactly one reason — the implementation does not exist yet. What the driver will see at BASE: 4 failing legs, two from (a) [M1] (line 625's filter keeps only 'BASE fact:', so both fact-line cases resolve to the BASE line alone) and two from (d) [M4] (neither fleet/RUNBOOK.md §Per run nor CLAUDE.md names 'STALE fact:'). Legs (b) [M2] and (c) [M3] are GREEN at BASE by design and that is not a gap: the task's own Context says the refusal path and renderLaunch are unchanged by this task and are pinned end to end so a later run cannot move them — (b) is the operator's laptop reading, (c) is the ordering the launch line owes the facts. Two readings a later session would otherwise reconstruct: (1) M1's 'in stdout order' is encoded as a second case answering the same two lines STALE-first and expecting them back STALE-first, so an implementation that sorts by kind (BASE lines then STALE lines) fails — the clause says stdout order, not a partition; (2) both Run: greps are re-expressed in process rather than shelled out, so the sim spawns nothing: sectionOf() reproduces sed -n '/^X/,/^Y/p' by taking the first line starting X through the next line starting Y (inclusive, as sed prints it) and joining on spaces the way tr '\n' ' ' does, then matches the same two regexes. Hermetic: imports are ../launch.mjs and ../lobby.mjs only, exec is a local recording async fn returning {code,stdout,stderr}, no spawn, no socket, no absolute literal outside the checkout, ends on ALL TESTS PASSED. Verified both ways: node fleet/tests/test_sims_are_hermetic.mjs stays green with the new sim present (26 sims swept, 0 offenders), and a scratch reference implementation (the line-625 filter widened plus the two doc sentences) turned the exam green before I reverted it — the tree I hand in carries only the exam file.

payload.body:
Exam written: tests/test_compile_plan_edges.py grows an appended section (436 lines, nothing above it touched — the eleven proof-run/Check: cases are byte-identical apart from two added imports, os and shutil). At BASE: 13 failed, 16 passed. Every failure reads as the absent evaluator — 'PLAN OK' / exit 0 where a 'STALE fact: ... holds at BASE' refusal was required, or no 'unreadable at BASE — ' advisory line where one was; (h) fails because the proof-gate section does not yet carry the two sentences. The 16 passes are the eleven existing cases plus the five rows whose predicate legitimately does not hold at BASE (path-exists on a missing file, path-absent on a present one, a foreign/absent sha, and M7's two no-base rows) — those five are the guard against an implementation that refuses everything.

Readings a later session would otherwise have to reconstruct:

1. (c) writes the entry exactly as the leg does: sha-matches: `present.py`@<id> — the backtick sits INSIDE, before the @. A naive .strip(' `') on the whole argument leaves 'present.py`' after the last-@ split and the path never resolves. The entry text is fixed by the leg, so the argument parse has to drop backticks everywhere in the argument, not just at its ends.

2. (f)'s two malformed rows are safe to compile at BASE: STALE_PREDICATE_RE (compile_plan.py:241) only matches head + colon, so 'issue-open: #' and 'sha-matches: `present.py`' parse into stale_if_entries without a grammar violation. The advisory path therefore never collides with the parser's own refusal.

3. The exam's plans are PLAN OK under --check --base at BASE (verified both ways), because the only base-gated refusal in collect_violations today is the Delete:-absent-at-BASE one (line 1727) and these plans carry no Delete:. That is what makes each holds-row red for exactly one reason.

4. M5's line is asserted by equality against a whole stdout line, with <entry> carrying its backticks as parse_task leaves it; M6's line only by its 'STALE fact: task <id>: <entry> unreadable at BASE — ' prefix, since the Context says nothing pins the reason's wording. The advisories are asserted to be on stdout AFTER the verdict (first stdout line == 'PLAN OK') and not counted in 'violation(s)'.

5. (d)'s once-per-number row gives task 1 issue-open: #538 and task 2 issue-closed: #538 — both name the number, exactly one holds under either answer, so one compile proves the cache (log has exactly one invocation) and both directions of M4 at once. The fake gh prints a file beside it and appends "$*" to a log; the no-gh PATH is a single dir holding only a symlink to the real git, which is enough for BaseTree's reads (confirmed: that compile still exits 0).
